diff_hunk:
@@ -95,7 +95,7 @@
 			<return type="Quaternion" />
 			<param index="0" name="euler" type="Vector3" />
 			<description>
-				Constructs a new [Quaternion] from the given [Vector3] of [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euler_angles]Euler angles[/url], in radians. This method always uses the YXZ convention ([constant EULER_ORDER_YXZ]).
+				Constructs a new [Quaternion] from the given [Vector3] of [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euler_angles]Euler angles[/url], in radians. In Godot, Euler angles always use intrinsic order. This method always uses the intrinsic YXZ convention ([constant EULER_ORDER_YXZ]): the first rotation is around the local Y axis (yaw), then local X (pitch), and lastly local Z (roll). When using the opposite method [method get_euler] to decompose a rotation, this order is reversed.
body: Not comfortable with recapping everything in the constructor, especially in the same first line. It duplicates information, it's a bit harder to localize, and if users are further interested they can look up the constant for further information.

body: There's no explanation anywhere about what "gimbal lock" is, so this is (to your dismay) something that sounds needlessly complicated to the average user. You could briefly link an explanation to it or not mention this concept at all.
